construction_note: This corpus is NOT pre-downloaded. Construct it from public Kaggle kernels via the Kaggle API/CLI. If credentials are missing, document the blocker instead of fabricating notebooks.

kaggle.auth_note: Prefer KAGGLE_API_TOKEN (injected from benchmark_credentials.yaml) or ~/.kaggle/access_token. Legacy kaggle.json also works.

construction_steps: Step 1 — Auth: KAGGLE_API_TOKEN is available in the container env (from benchmark credentials). Fallback files: /shared/kaggle/access_token or kaggle.json.
Step 2 — Search: For each target function, list kernels with `kaggle kernels list -s <name>`.
Step 3 — Download: Pull candidate .ipynb / .Rmd kernels and their public datasets.
Step 4 — Filter: Keep notebooks with real call sites, public data, runtime <10 minutes, no non-trivial errors.
Step 5 — Persist: Save under dataset_candidate/kaggle_notebooks/{python,r}/ with a manifest.json listing kernel id, language, functions used, and run status.

recommended_scale.note: Full paper uses 128 notebooks. Use a reduced subset for a single benchmark run.
recommended_scale.minimal: 20 Python notebooks covering ttest_ind, ttest_1samp, f_oneway, linregress
